baseline.scope: Linux feature preservation; source inventory, not live acceptance

status_policy.not_integrated: Feature is in migration scope; no complete routerd2 compatibility/behavior acceptance is recorded.
status_policy.partial_native_primitives: Kernel operations exist but do not implement the original resource fields, orchestration or control/API behavior.
complete_requires: protocol and packet interoperability where applicable
version-coherent bundled module lifecycle without Ubuntu/systemd dependency
status_policy.unknown_input: Reject unknown kinds/fields or unsupported known capability explicitly before mutation; never omit them from a successful plan.

modules.native_replacement: Keep typed resources, merge/override/provenance and validation. Compile bundled plugin capabilities to explicit module calls. An arbitrary executable is an explicit compatibility boundary, never silently ignored.
modules.known_gap: PluginSpec.Executable and plugin.Runner currently launch external programs. A generic arbitrary executable cannot be made equivalent merely by mapping its path to routerd.

modules.native_replacement: Read/write validated procfs settings, use hostname syscall, and satisfy package intent through versioned image/module capabilities. Preserve original intent and return a compatibility error for an unmapped package.
modules.known_gap: Package is still public input; SystemdUnit, KernelModule and NetworkAdoption are already removed public kinds. Their derived internal jobs must become supervisor/kernel-module operations.

modules.native_replacement: Retain structured event/log storage, OTLP exporters and retention; feed them from owned worker pipes, netlink/NFLOG and typed diagnostics. Embed optional DPI engine with explicit build and license metadata.
modules.known_gap: Independent journald-free structured logging is implemented. Original LogSink/Telemetry/OTLP/flow/NFLOG/DPI contracts and full retention/export APIs remain incomplete. nDPI is an optional C/CGO engine.

modules.native_replacement: Preserve control operation semantics and inspection views; serve embedded static assets and use native kernel/module observations. Add SSH command sessions to the same typed control interface.
modules.known_gap: Native revisioned configuration/SSH, bounded mutation acknowledgements, lightweight health and explicit paged observations are integrated. Original resource apply/delete, probes, logs, federation and complete operational views remain incomplete.

modules.native_replacement: Retain HA policy and lifecycle; implement VRRP worker with native packet/socket/VIP effects and transfer typed lease/session snapshots and deltas over authenticated peer transport.
modules.known_gap: Native VRRPv3 IPv4/IPv6, explicit IPv4 VRRPv2 with optional PASS, and declared-resource Health/BFD/BGP tracking are implemented. Explicit false conditions produce finite neutral decisions that retain counts and penalty. Other resource kinds and Disabled/NotApplicable/Standby phase contracts, external secret resolution and peer-aware legacy import, symmetric native HA qualification, cluster dependency gating, lease replication and NAT session replication remain incomplete. Additional MAC/link-local identities are expressed by conditional network resources with independent writer fencing and scoped L2 announcements.

modules.native_replacement: Compile interface alias, bridge membership, VLAN/VXLAN and VRF intent to typed rtnetlink operations with per-resource ownership.
modules.known_gap: Native bridge/VLAN/VRF/VXLAN/macvlan/dummy, alias and membership ownership are implemented. Owned dummy sources and IPv4/IPv6 routing domains with identical endpoint addresses run with actual daemon BFD/BGP and independent TCP/UDP peers. Full legacy lifecycle, link options, automatic IPv6 link-local DAD startup, forwarding policy, dependency and adoption semantics still need per-resource acceptance.

modules.native_replacement: Retain address selection, PD suffix calculation, dependencies and lifetime policy; feed typed address desired state to the native engine.
modules.known_gap: Native static, DHCP/PD finite/deprecated addresses and VRRP VMAC address ownership are implemented. Full SelfAddressPolicy and legacy dependency semantics remain incomplete. Native RA facts and restart now retain original boot deadlines; real RA/backend TCP/UDP and guest UTC correction gates pass. Complete resource behavior and physical suspend remain unqualified.

modules.native_replacement: Retain candidate selection and health policy; emit typed routes, rule priorities, marks, multipath/source-hash selectors and MTU/MSS effects.
modules.known_gap: Native scalar/ECMP routes, policy rules and BGP next-hop projection are implemented. Cluster/egress health selection, MTU/MSS and force-fragment behavior remain incomplete.

modules.native_replacement: Retain native probes, interface/DS-Lite binding, timers and status events as supervised workers.
Reuse native DHCPv4 protocol engine and lease journal; replace command-line process entry with self-reexec worker and netlink lease effects.
One native DHCPv6 client owns IA_NA, IA_PD and information on a shared interface socket; typed assignments feed the sole network writer and generated RA.
modules.known_gap: One native client owns IA_NA/IA_PD/information and their original BOOTTIME budgets. Control no longer creates a receipt grant. RA router/prefix/DNS and AFTR preserve original deadlines; AFTR no longer copies/rebases its input or maintains wall-clock anchors. Independent dnsmasq covers IA_NA lifecycle, and independent wire/real-daemon tests cover combined IA_NA/IA_PD, renumbering, LAN RA/TCP/UDP, expiry and recovery. A dedicated no-NIC QEMU passed actual UTC +/-24h, frozen producer snapshots, continued LAN communication, original writer address expiry with control/supervisor frozen, bounded/withdrawn RA, expired delivery replay and fresh acquisition. Independent dnsmasq plus a Linux duplicate host verified actual finite-address DAD failure/Decline, withdrawal and usable replacement TCP/UDP on the same worker; the client now consumes kernel notifications instead of polling an already-deleted address. Complete resource selection/readiness, DAD coexistence with other IA_NA/IA_PD bindings, Release, RA trigger/resolver effects, actual suspend/reboot, VRF and hardware remain incomplete. Actual uplink PD /60 acquisition and delegated LAN IPv6 TCP/UDP succeeded after removing a port-547 receive restriction and waiting for normal link-local DAD. Actual T1=7200-second renewal, rebind, expiry and Release are not qualified.

modules.native_replacement: Retain config/status/event behavior; provide discovery, PPP authentication/LCP/IPCP/IPv6CP and kernel PPP attachment in an owned protocol worker.
modules.known_gap: The existing client constructs pppd/FreeBSD ppp commands. Wrapping that client in a self-reexec worker does not replace the PPP engine.

modules.native_replacement: Retain AFTR resolution and self-address selection; emit native ip6tnl, tunnel-address, policy-route and MTU plans.
modules.known_gap: Native B4 and AFTR resolution consume explicit RA/DHCPv6 dependencies with original DNS/source deadlines. Static and generated tunnels use ordinary ip6tnl ownership. An independent RA sender, DNS, Linux AFTR and separate LAN client verified actual daemon NAT/IPv4-in-IPv6 TCP/UDP, original RDNSS and preferred-source expiry with control stopped, expired notification without resurrection, renumbering recovery and RA/network worker replacement. The bootstrap firewall now accepts interface-name selectors before the dynamic link exists. SelfAddressPolicy, multi-AFTR source routing, full resource readiness/lifecycle, suspend/reboot, VRF and hardware remain incomplete. Actual uplink RA lifetime renewal and DNS RRset rotation reproduced tunnel recreation and TCP loss. Query generations now track endpoint identity, current budgets cap projection immediately, and refreshed DNS retains a still-answered remote. Final actual-AFTR LAN HTTPS/UDP survived 100 seconds on one TCP connection, with an unchanged tunnel index for 110 seconds. Long real-lease renewal and complete source-selection qualification remain open.

modules.native_replacement: Preserve all declared scopes, reservations, options, profiles, sticky assignments, lease events and RA lifetimes; implement server/relay/RA workers and typed lease store.
modules.known_gap: Native RA server/client, delegated-prefix updates and DHCPv4 server are implemented. Generated RA is verified with an independent PD peer, actual LAN PIO capture, renew/renumber on the same worker, owned expiry/reacquisition and routed client TCP/UDP. Native DHCPv4 relay now has independent dnsmasq/BusyBox DORA on two LANs, unicast/broadcast replies, DHCPINFORM, hop-limit discard, worker recovery and client TCP/UDP. Oversized unicast/broadcast DHCP replies now fragment at the LAN MTU; independent peers and kernel reassembly preserve two 200-byte options on MTU 600. Independent blue/red/default domains with identical endpoints now pass DHCP/TCP/UDP and relay retirement/recovery. Actual ingress-domain validation prevents a late reply crossing into the default LAN with udp_l3mdev_accept enabled. DHCPv6 server, relay HA and dynamic-domain qualification, complete dynamic dependencies, original global sticky behavior and lease-sync resource semantics remain incomplete.

modules.native_replacement: Extract the native resolver main package into an engine worker while preserving zone/forward/upstream behavior, binding, failover, aliases, cache and query logging.
Reuse GoBGP v4 engine, policies, IPv4 unicast mobility path handling and native Linux FIB adapter; supervise worker and preserve route ownership/withdrawal and status semantics.
modules.known_gap: Extracted GoBGP v4 engine, dual-stack policy, route effects and durable dynamic-path API are integrated. An explicit native BFD dependency passed consumer and real two-binary QEMU failure/recovery gates. Original BFD profile/resource and SAM controller orchestration, mobility ownership policy and resource conversion remain incomplete. EVPN is deferred in the original baseline and is not a prerequisite for parity with it.

modules.native_replacement: Retain BFD config and peer integration; replace vtysh/FRR execution with an owned BFD protocol engine and typed session events.
modules.known_gap: Native active asynchronous IPv4/IPv6 BFD supports explicit single-hop interface scope, routed multihop endpoint pairs and VRF scope without FRR/vtysh. IPv4/IPv6 real-daemon multihop checks use the same endpoints in two VRFs and the default domain simultaneously. Receive-only address reuse fixes their UDP bind collision while per-domain abstract claims retain exclusive routerd ownership. Original resource profiles, dynamic source selection, full controller/status/lifecycle contracts, automatic link-local DAD startup, IPv6 single-hop VRF, authentication and other unsupported modes remain incomplete.

modules.native_replacement: Keep peer resolution and enrollment policy; use kernel WireGuard generic netlink/wgctrl semantics plus rtnetlink routes instead of wg setconf.
modules.known_gap: Native kernel generic-netlink WireGuard, complete peer sets, encrypted traffic, immutable key snapshots, endpoint roaming and failure quarantine are implemented. Strict static peer/file-key conversion and supported original listener-firewall policy are available. Peer hostname resolution, SAM/enrollment, standalone fixed-listener conversion without an owned INPUT filter and complete resource lifecycle semantics remain incomplete.

modules.native_replacement: Retain connection/secret policy; select and integrate an IKE engine with native XFRM programming, SA lifecycle and operational status.
modules.known_gap: Current implementation invokes strongSwan swanctl. XFRM alone does not implement IKE negotiation, authentication, rekey or interoperability.

modules.native_replacement: Integrate a compatible Tailscale engine/control client and preserve routing/auth/state behavior through a dedicated module API.
modules.known_gap: Current code invokes tailscaled/tailscale. A userspace proxy or basic tsnet connection is not automatically exit-node, subnet-router and CLI feature parity.

modules.native_replacement: Reuse provider action policy, approval/journal model and tunnel planners; implement native tunnel effects and provider HTTP/SDK adapters behind typed contracts.
modules.known_gap: Provider executors are external programs. Preserve cloud-specific operation idempotency, verification, rollback and credentials; replacing CLI invocation with an SDK call alone is insufficient.

modules.native_replacement: Reuse SAM discovery/ownership, enrollment, transport generation, shard planning and BGP delivery logic; translate typed dataplane plans to owned Linux effectors.
modules.known_gap: Include cloud capture, ARP fanout, leases, fencing, enrollment revocation, route convergence, retry/outbox and diagnostics; do not reduce SAM to tunnel creation.

modules.native_replacement: Reuse authenticated transport, durable outbox/consumer state, replay/idempotency and subscription semantics; use module capability calls for generated actions.
Reuse event operators, durable consumption, dependency evaluation and resource status publication; preserve event schemas and timing behavior.
Preserve semantic rule/policy decisions, automatic service holes, source selection, TTL sets, DNAT/SNAT, ingress health/drain and pinholes; compile typed expressions into owned nftables batches.
modules.known_gap: Baseline native filter and masquerade do not cover full legacy stateful, L2, policy, ingress, set, logging or NAT semantics. Do not translate arbitrary nft text into partial rules silently.

modules.native_replacement: Preserve static/DHCP time-source selection and server policy; implement or integrate a time discipline engine with adjtimex/clock operations and supervised NTP service.
modules.known_gap: One-shot SNTP clock setting is not chrony/timesyncd client/server behavior or oscillator discipline parity.

boundary_findings.finding: Render returns []render.File. Retain declaration extraction; replace file rendering with typed link/address/route effects.
Ruleset stores Path/Data; Diff compares file bytes and Reload invokes nft -c/-f. Replace with semantic rule IR and netlink compilation.
Service manager returns executable/argv plans. Replace with module desired instances, not a fake systemctl command parser.
Options injects selected external binary paths/runners and dry-run flags, not a universal kernel or supervisor interface. Many effects bypass any global runner.
Reuse resource-to-service spec knowledge for DNS, DHCPv4, DHCPv6, PPPoE and ARP worker compilation. Existing specs still name separate binaries and can contain secrets in argv.
Spec validation/socket readiness helper only. The actual existing supervision logic lives in chain.go.
Local Command and CommandStdin test ports exist; chain wiring does not populate them. Replace backend operations at typed configuration boundary.
Plain yaml.Unmarshal plus custom resource Decode is not strict unknown-field validation. Add strict recursive typed validation before compilation and preserve raw input/provenance.
Keep explicit migration errors for removed input kinds. Do not reintroduce SystemdUnit as a compatibility escape hatch.
Arbitrary external plugin executable behavior needs explicit module conversion, a supported packaged engine, or a compatibility error.
Preserve approval, verification, journal and rollback semantics while replacing executable provider adapters with owned typed adapters.
The current PPPoE client builds a pppd/ppp command; it is not a native PPP protocol engine.
Connection application depends on strongSwan swanctl; native XFRM plumbing alone cannot replace IKE.
Linux VRRP uses keepalived backend; controller reuse does not provide protocol execution.
The kernel provides the data plane; replace wg tool with generic netlink control while retaining peer-resolution policy.
Current operational status invokes tailscale; full control and forwarding behavior still requires an integrated engine.
WebConsole already embeds built frontend assets; Node/npm are build-time dependencies, not necessary runtime utilities.

inventory_limits: Static source inventory does not prove every declared upstream feature has been validated live.
Direct spec fields are navigation metadata; nested schemas/defaults/constraints must be preserved from the schema and typed definitions, not reconstructed from this list.
CLI dispatch and advertised syntax are inventoried; every flag and output field still needs compatibility tests.
Decoder-only kinds are not a claim that user-declared config validation accepts them.
No feature becomes complete by copying source or compiling a binary; semantic and runtime acceptance evidence is required.

routerd2_native_primitives.validation: Unit and race tests passed. QEMU Linux packet gates passed for IPv4/IPv6 forwarding, NAT44/NAT66 masquerade, DS-Lite TCP and peer addresses, ECMP, policy routes, bridge/VLAN/VRF/VXLAN/macvlan, finite/deprecated address lifetimes and VRRP input guards. QEMU packet gates also passed IPv4/IPv6 INPUT/OUTPUT/FORWARD ACLs, ICMP rejection, established-flow preservation and DNAT/SNAT/masquerade with translated port ranges. Native WireGuard no-NIC QEMU passed encrypted IPv4/IPv6 traffic and outer endpoints, handshake/counters, roaming, multipart replacement and partial failure, journal rollback, PSK/peer removal, foreign-state preservation, UP acknowledgement loss and independent cancellation quarantine. Private key publication passed abrupt-process-exit/retry tests at five durability boundaries. The network API acknowledges apply without echoing oversized observation snapshots. Capacity fixtures passed with 16,000 routes and 30,000 WireGuard allowed IPs, including exact scoped counts, explicit truncation, escaped JSON byte bounds, nested detail pages, indexed route ownership and intent projection fences. Network summaries/pages are bounded to 256 KiB; desired chunks are bounded to 64 KiB with a 2 MiB complete-document bound. Detail pages are fresh observations, not an atomic cross-page kernel snapshot. These synthetic counts are response-capacity evidence, not a packet-throughput qualification.

Unit/race plus fresh network namespace acquisition, renewal and expiry against an independent DHCP server passed. Runtime projection/fencing/rollback and conflicting static-address ownership tests passed.

Unit/race and fresh namespace native-client DORA, T1 renewal, journal restart INIT-REBOOT, independent wire NAK/RELEASE/DECLINE and pre-address Ethernet unicast passed. Durable journal and coordinator ACK precede client ACK. Actual two-binary daemon DHCP-to-DNS expiry/recovery passed.

Original BOOTTIME assignment, information and exchange budgets now replace UTC lease deadlines. Actual no-NIC QEMU UTC +/-24h with frozen producer/control/supervisor passed unchanged original observations, LAN TCP/UDP, writer IA_NA/LAN address expiry, bounded/withdrawn RA, expired replay and fresh acquisition. Native PD/RA and independent DNS/AFTR namespace gates also passed. Independent dnsmasq/Linux duplicate-host DAD/Decline, withdrawal and usable replacement TCP/UDP passed on the same actual worker. Full resource/phase parity, actual suspend/reboot, DAD coexistence with other bindings, Release, VRF and hardware remain open.
Unit/race and real multicast/RS tests passed for lifetime encoding, same-socket live prefix updates, selective withdrawal, invalid-update rejection and shutdown withdrawal.

Unit/race plus independent native IPv4 and IPv6 peer elections/failover passed. Kernel VMAC, explicit NoDAD, input guards and monotonic ownership-expiry projection are tested. Original v2/auth/tracking/cluster dependency behavior remains separate.

Unit/race and native UDP/TCP/DoT/DoH/DoQ tests passed. Real two-binary daemon and embedded SSH test changes answers, confirms configuration, rolls back unconfirmed changes and recovers after SIGKILL of control/logging. Source-scoped typed DHCP A/PTR updates, finite TTL and producer ownership expiry passed. The full two-binary daemon preserves the DNS process and TCP connection through DHCP SIGSTOP/expiry/SIGKILL/journal recovery.

Unit/race plus independent TCP peers passed IPv4/IPv6 policy, advertisement and withdrawal. Real two-binary daemon tests install and withdraw protocol242 kernel FIB routes, report unresolved next hops without speculative onlink routes, repair them, and expire ownership while the BGP worker is SIGSTOPped. Recursive/ECMP/VRF/link-local resolution tests also passed. The explicit native peer_bfd consumer passed pure/race identity, deadline, actual admin-ACK, RIB-version and per-reset withdrawal-ACK fences. TestBFDWireExpiryClosesActualTCPWhileRouteEffectsBlocked passed actual TCP closure while route effects were blocked. The real two-binary daemon-bfd QEMU gate passed startup suppression, UDP-only loss, suspended-worker receive expiry and fresh BGP/FIB recovery; this does not establish original BGPPeer.bfd/profile or BFD resource compatibility.

routerd2_native_primitives.scope: Native active asynchronous IPv4/IPv6 BFD. Single-hop owns one explicit interface/family; multihop owns one committed local source address, including loopback endpoints with independently routed egress. Each worker has up to 64 configured peers. BGP consumes finite typed health; BFD creates no routes.
routerd2_native_primitives.validation: PVE isolated Linux VM: make check-bfd passed the current single-hop BFD/BGP daemon case, routed IPv4 BFD/BGP failure/recovery/expiry and routed IPv6 BFD loss/recovery/worker replacement. Routed packet captures verify UDP 4784, source ports, outgoing TTL/Hop Limit 255 and incoming 254 across a real Linux forwarder. Local checks retain single-hop TTL, device scope, discriminators, original clocks, source lifecycle and source/recipient fences. This is not target hardware, authenticated BFD, or full original resource parity. Routed IPv4 user TCP/UDP crosses the learned prefix, fails while that route is withdrawn and resumes after BFD/BGP recovery.

acceptance_gates.scope: Executed native daemon and actual kernel communication; current routed modes have not run in QEMU or on physical devices.

limitations: Authentication, echo execution and demand/passive modes remain unimplemented; BFD-bound BGP rejects graceful restart.
Multihop requires explicit committed non-link-local endpoints and no interface binding. Dynamic source selection, VRF routing context and original BFD resource/profile lifecycle remain incomplete.
FIB withdrawal uses the existing network writer and reconciliation schedule. No hard realtime, target hardware, suspend or scale qualification is claimed.

routerd2_native_primitives.validation: Unit/race tests passed queue bounds, collector restart, disk failure and slow fallback. Real-daemon SIGKILL of logging leaves DNS available. Journald is not a runtime dependency.

Pinned legacy schema decoding, strict field/reference rejection, deterministic conversion and parser fuzz passed. Explicit WAN policies carry replacement notes; PD/information aliasing and dynamic RA/AFTR/B4 peer/gateway graphs passed the public Runtime boundary with expiry and fencing. CLI policy migration writes no configuration on compile failure. Unsupported inputs still reject the entire graph. Static DHCPv4Server/DHCPv4Reservation and WireGuardInterface/WireGuardPeer subsets are compiled with complete-failure diagnostics, explicit static ownership and supported original defaults. DHCP-derived DNS requires each resolver to authorize source-scoped finite lease behavior; public Runtime.Accept-to-DNSLeases tests cover source isolation, digest fencing, producer expiry, replay, recovery and removal. Packet-decision fixtures preserve untrust DHCP server UDP/67 ordering, WireGuard listener scoping and authoritative DNS/trust/mgmt ACLs. These are partial resource contracts, not full semantic parity. The actual two-binary daemon-legacy-dhcp-dns QEMU gate passed migrated DHCP ACK and DNS publication, stopped-producer expiry, durable restart recovery and preservation of the existing DNS process/TCP connection; the untrust fixture retained the original scoped UDP/67 exception before its explicit deny ACL.
limitations: Original resource lifecycle, when/dependsOn/ready_when, dynamic config/SAM/HA and arbitrary external ownership remain unsupported.
Positive legacy stickyHoldDays and lease-file import are rejected; native per-worker sticky behavior does not reproduce the original family-wide sticky contract.
Static WireGuard requires explicit file-key paths and numeric/passive endpoints; nonzero listenPort without an owned INPUT filter is rejected instead of adding an unrelated conntrack drop.
